amends: bench-v1.1 (configs/benchmark_protocol_v1.json, unchanged; every metric definition, parameter and the v1.1 metric-level tables stay as they are)
status: pre-registered in frozen/benchmark_protocol_v1.2.sha256 before any protocol metric was computed on an evaluation dataset, and written without opening any TrajPE or baseline result (the map follows from the metric definitions of configs/benchmark_protocol_v1.json only)
purpose: The v1.1 headline counts every primary metric as an independent cell, but several primary metrics compare the same statistic of the same data with a different binning, grid, divergence or query set (travel distance x5, diameter x4, Kendall tau x3, pattern support x4, ...). bench-v1.2 groups the primary metrics into statistic families, counts each family once per dataset x epsilon, and adds a verdict per source paper on that paper's own metrics. The v1.1 metric-level tables are still reported unchanged; the v1.2 family-level headline is the primary headline from bench-v1.2 on.

family_rule.same_family: two primary metrics belong to one family when they compare the same empirical distribution (same unit of observation and same variables) with the same kind of comparison
family_rule.ignored: resolution (grid size, cell vs venue, number of bins or buckets, bucket range), divergence (JSD variant, smoothing), squared vs plain distance, joint vs start-conditional form of the same pair of variables, query shape and number, top-k size and pattern lengths, tie conventions, counting a pattern by occurrences or by trajectories that contain it, and time-of-day vs time-of-week resolution
family_rule.units: check-in point; hop (consecutive check-in pair); trail; trail coverage (trail x region incidence); pattern (contiguous cell sub-sequence); time-located point
family_rule.time_split: a metric whose statistic includes a time variable (timestamp window, time of day/week) is not in the same family as its time-free counterpart
family_rule.next_poi: one family per downstream model (transformer, markov): its 7 primary metrics (acc@1, acc@5, acc@10, acc@20, ndcg@5, ndcg@10, mrr, scope last) are rankings of the same predictions
family_rule.excluded: variants (movesim_grank_rank, movesim_irank_rank, llmob_si_code, llmob_dard_code, llmob_stvd_code), duplicates (ldp_trip_error, retra_trip_error), next-POI scope 'all' and next-POI models that are not registered in the protocol are reported in the v1.1 tables only

step_distance.variables: distance between consecutive locations (MoveSim squares it)

origin_destination.kind: distribution divergence (AdaTrace joint, HRNet conditional on the 30 most frequent starts)

step_interval.variables: time between consecutive check-ins (MoveSim merges consecutive check-ins at one venue into a stay)

venue_popularity.variables: visit probabilities of the most visited venues

nextpoi_transformer.variables: next-POI predictions of the transformer trained on the release

nextpoi_markov.variables: next-POI predictions of the Markov model trained on the release

paper_suites.rule: a paper's suite is the primary metrics whose source_paper is that paper (configs/benchmark_protocol_v1.json); next-POI belongs to Massive-STEPS; the code checks that this list equals the source_paper field

statistics.metric_difference: per (dataset, eps, primary metric) and baseline: the bench-v1.1 normalized difference d = (loss_baseline - loss_TrajPE) / (loss_baseline + loss_TrajPE) in [-1, 1] on seed means (scale-free; d > 0 means TrajPE is better)
statistics.family_score: D = unweighted mean of d over the family's primary metrics that both methods have in that dataset x eps (restricted to the metric subset of the summary, e.g. unmeasured only); a family cell with no such metric is absent
statistics.family_counts: win if D > 0, loss if D < 0, tie if |D| <= 1e-12 (by seed means; no per-cell test)
statistics.headline: per baseline over all family cells both methods have: W/T/L, median D, Wilcoxon signed-rank test on D (two-sided, zeros dropped; primary test) and sign test (two-sided binomial; secondary), each Holm-corrected over baselines. TrajPE beats a baseline on the headline iff Holm-Wilcoxon p < 0.05 and the median of the non-tied D (the values the test uses) is > 0; loses iff p < 0.05 and that median is < 0; otherwise no significant difference (n.s., with the sign of the win/loss majority)
statistics.ranks: per family cell and method: mean of the method's per-metric ranks (by loss, ties averaged) over the family's metrics that every compared method has, re-ranked within the family cell (ties averaged); average over the family cells where every method is present; Friedman test and Nemenyi CD with N = number of such family cells
statistics.per_paper: per baseline and paper suite: the suite's primary metrics are grouped into the families above (restricted to the suite), giving family cells (dataset, eps, family); W/T/L and median D over them, Wilcoxon (primary) and sign test, Holm over the 8 suites within each baseline; also the paper-cell score (mean of the suite's family D per dataset x eps) with its W/T/L. Verdict: as the headline, on the suite's family cells: 'win' iff Holm-Wilcoxon p < 0.05 and the median of the non-tied D > 0, 'loss' iff p < 0.05 and it is < 0, otherwise 'n.s.' with the sign of the family-cell win/loss majority
statistics.v3_split: the family summaries are repeated for the near + unmeasured, unmeasured-only and measured subsets of bench-v1.1 (Section 6): the metric subset is applied first, then families are formed from the remaining metrics
statistics.outputs: with scripts/bench_tables.py --families configs/benchmark_protocol_v1.2_families.json: tables_families.md, family_cells.csv and summary_families.json next to the unchanged v1.1 outputs; without --families the output is byte-identical to bench-v1.1
